short_definition: A security framework where cloud providers and customers share accountability for system security.
layman_explanation: The cloud provider secures the apartment building infrastructure, but you are still responsible for locking your own front door.

short_definition: A misconfiguration in cloud storage allowing unauthenticated public internet access to private files.
layman_explanation: Leaving a filing cabinet in a public park unlocked instead of inside a secure office building.

short_definition: Automated tools that continuously monitor cloud environments to detect misconfigurations and compliance violations.
layman_explanation: An automated building inspector continuously checking every door, window, and fire exit across all your properties.

short_definition: Securing applications that rely on ephemeral function executions rather than persistent virtual servers.
layman_explanation: Renting a kitchen by the minute to cook one meal, requiring brief but tight security checks for every single dish.

short_definition: An exploit where a user breaks out of an isolated application container onto the underlying host operating system.
layman_explanation: A hotel guest finding a secret doorway out of their private room into the hotel's central control hub.

short_definition: A security enforcement point placed between users and cloud services to enforce organizational policies.
layman_explanation: A border checkpoint inspecting every package traveling between your office network and external cloud services.

short_definition: Short-lived cloud components created dynamically and destroyed as soon as their job is finished.
layman_explanation: Using temporary disposable cell phones instead of landline phones so attackers have no persistent target.

short_definition: A network security technique that isolates individual workloads and limits internal lateral traffic.
layman_explanation: Putting individual steel doors between every single office cubicle so an intruder cannot move between desks.

short_definition: Hardware or software used within an organization without IT team knowledge or authorization.
layman_explanation: Employees bringing unapproved home tools into a factory to complete work faster without safety checks.

short_definition: Scanning cloud deployment scripts for security vulnerabilities before infrastructure is provisioned.
layman_explanation: Checking architectural blueprints for structural flaws before building materials are purchased.

short_definition: An architecture where multiple customers share the same physical server resources safely separated logically.
layman_explanation: Different families living in adjacent apartments inside one apartment building using separate locks.

short_definition: Inspecting network traffic exiting a private cloud environment to prevent data exfiltration.
layman_explanation: Security guards inspecting backpacks of people leaving a store rather than checking incoming shoppers.

short_definition: A unified platform combining cloud security scanning, container protection, and posture management.
layman_explanation: A single master security control center monitoring CCTV, smoke alarms, and keycards across all cloud sites.

short_definition: A management tool enforcing authentication, rate limits, and routing between cloud clients and backends.
layman_explanation: A central mailroom routing incoming packages to internal departments while verifying sender credentials.

short_definition: Legal and compliance requirements specifying physical geographic locations where data must be stored.
layman_explanation: Rules mandating that official bank documents must remain inside country borders and cannot be transferred overseas.
